q: A Bhilwara textile mill runs its own coal power plant: how does that change its footprint?
title: Bhilwara mills with captive coal power
short: Coal burned in your captive plant is Scope 1, counted from tonnes and calorific value on your coal invoices. Power you then use is not Scope 2 again. Per kWh, an old small coal unit is often worse than the grid at 0.710 (FY 2024-25 grid factor) kg, so the comparison is worth making.
audience: Spinning, weaving and processing mills in Bhilwara with captive thermal power

ul: Coal or lignite invoices with tonnes and GCV.
Units generated and units used by the mill.
Any power sold or wheeled to the grid.

ol: Coal CO2 ÷ units generated = your own kg per kWh.
Compare with the grid factor, 0.710 on CEA v21.0.
Add open access solar or wind to see the mix.

p: Brands ask for footprint per kg of yarn or per metre of fabric. Captive coal often decides it, so show it separately.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so each figure you send a buyer traces back to the documents behind it.
